Let me produce the final report. # Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information - **Prow Job**: pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-images - **Build ID**: 2075251150172459008 - **Target**: images - **PR**: #8967 (NO-JIRA: chore: update core-reviewers membership) - **Cluster**: build01 ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` error occurred handling build hypershift-amd64: the build hypershift-amd64 failed after 3m21s with reason DockerBuildFailed: Dockerfile build strategy has failed. error: build error: creating build container: copying system blob sha256:9b6302bf389d9ada149f967a1f6feb319b4e0747b92f8244b2f5a6996032bf6b: received unexpected HTTP status: 503 Service Unavailable ``` ### Summary The `hypershift-amd64` image build (from `Dockerfile.control-plane`) failed during its second stage (`[2/2] STEP 1/22`) when the build pod attempted to pull the base image `ocp_4.23_base-rhel9` (`quay-proxy.ci.openshift.org/openshift/ci@sha256:9b6302bf...`). The container registry returned an HTTP 503 Service Unavailable error. This is a transient CI infrastructure failure completely unrelated to the PR's code change, which only modifies the `OWNERS_ALIASES` file. All other builds in the same job (`hypershift-operator-amd64`, `hypershift-tests-amd64`, `hypershift-cli-amd64`, `src-amd64`) completed successfully. A simple retest should pass.
Root Cause The root cause is a **transient HTTP 503 error from the `quay-proxy.ci.openshift.org` container image registry**. During the `hypershift-amd64` build (which uses `Dockerfile.control-plane`, a multi-stage Dockerfile), Stage 1 (`builder`) completed successfully — both `control-plane-operator` and `control-plane-pki-operator` binaries were compiled. However, when Stage 2 (`[2/2] STEP 1/22`) attempted to pull the runtime base image `ocp_4.23_base-rhel9` at `quay-proxy.ci.openshift.org/openshift/ci@sha256:9b6302bf389d9ada149f967a1f6feb319b4e0747b92f8244b2f5a6996032bf6b`, the registry proxy returned a 503 Service Unavailable response. Notably, the **same image** was successfully pre-cached earlier in the build (lines 71–79 of build-log.txt at ~16:21:27Z), and other builds in the same job that pulled from the same registry (including `hypershift-operator-amd64` which uses the same `Dockerfile.control-plane`'s builder stage and a similar runtime base) all succeeded. This confirms the 503 was a momentary registry availability glitch, not a persistent outage. The PR itself only modifies `OWNERS_ALIASES` (a reviewer assignment config file) and makes zero changes to any Dockerfile, Go source code, or build configuration. The failure is entirely infrastructure-related and not caused by the PR.
Recommendations 1. **Retest the PR** — Run `/retest` or `/test images` on the PR. This is a transient infrastructure flake and should pass on retry. 2. **No code changes needed** — The PR (which only updates `OWNERS_ALIASES`) is not related to the failure in any way. 3. **If the failure recurs**, it would indicate a persistent issue with the `quay-proxy.ci.openshift.org` registry proxy and should be reported to the CI infrastructure team (Test Platform / DPTP).
Evidence | Evidence | Detail | |----------|--------| | Failed build | `hypershift-amd64` (Dockerfile.control-plane) — failed at Stage 2 (`[2/2] STEP 1/22`) | | Error message | `creating build container: copying system blob sha256:9b6302bf...: received unexpected HTTP status: 503 Service Unavailable` | | Failed image pull | `quay-proxy.ci.openshift.org/openshift/ci@sha256:9b6302bf389d9ada149f967a1f6feb319b4e0747b92f8244b2f5a6996032bf6b` (ocp_4.23_base-rhel9) | | Build timing | Started 16:19:53Z, failed at 16:23:14Z (3m21s) | | Same image pre-cached OK | The identical image was successfully pulled at ~16:21:27Z during build setup (lines 71–79 of build-log.txt) | | Other builds succeeded | `hypershift-operator-amd64` (5m40s ✅), `hypershift-tests-amd64` (12m40s ✅), `hypershift-cli-amd64` (1m40s ✅), `src-amd64` (2m43s ✅) | | PR changes | Only `OWNERS_ALIASES` — zero Dockerfile, Go, or build config changes | | Failure reason | `DockerBuildFailed` — transient registry 503, not a code or config issue |
